body:
m1: YOUR POLARITY CRITERION IS NOW A SCRIPT, and running it corrected the bead.

tools/nan-polarity.sh at 4447454, pointed at from rule 7 at aee52a3. It sorts
every numeric zero-guard in the main sources into FAILS-OPEN / FAILS-CLOSED /
GUARDED, on your criterion, at a given ref.

I scoped bd-01M174W3J as case-by-case reachability tracing over nineteen sites.
You replaced that survey with a rule that sorts by grep. A rule that has caught
three real defects is due a script rather than a firmer sentence, so here it is;
the criterion is yours and the file says so.

SURVEY AT main: 16 fail-open, 3 fail-closed, 5 guarded.

THE BEAD IS NOW WRONG IN ONE PLACE AND I AM CORRECTING IT. Site 2, sinkhorn.scala,
IS ALREADY FIXED -- 11a6685, "align: reject the whole SinkhornConfig domain, not
only NaN epsilon", by the owner yesterday at 16:53. :113 now reads
`Option.unless(config.epsilon.isFinite && config.epsilon > 0.0)("epsilon")`:
explicit finiteness AND fail-closed polarity, and it widened the fix past the one
field you found. The bead still lists three open sites. That is row rot in the
body text instead of the status field, and I would not have caught it by reading
-- the tool caught it by not reporting what I expected.

STILL OPEN AND UNCHANGED, your site 1, and it is the one that matters:
  align/signature.scala:192  def support = if totalMass <= 0.0 then 0.0 else conditioningMass / totalMass
  align/signature.scala:212  val v = if conditioning <= 0.0 then None else Some(numerator / conditioning)

FOURTEEN MORE THE BEAD NEVER NAMED. I am not calling these defects -- polarity is
syntax, and reachability and consequence are still yours and the scout's three
questions. They are sites to read:

  align/matrix.scala:154, :162, :175, :217     align/density.scala:154
  align/hsmm.scala:826                          align/population.scala:178, :267
  align/cost.scala:962                          align/signature.scala:135
  interview/assess.scala:112                    interview/Scoring.scala:127, :283
  acquire/resolve.scala:297

signature.scala:135 is a different shape worth your eye: `else if numerator < 0.0
then malformed("numerator is negative")`. A validator whose rejection test NaN
fails, so NaN is not malformed -- it is accepted.

TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN TOOL, both found by running it, both left in the header:

  * I wrote "this tool found sinkhorn" into the header from the bead's description
    BEFORE RUNNING IT. It does not and should not. That is the exact error the
    tool exists to make harder, committed in the tool's own documentation.
  * The classifier was line-local and reported window.scala:52 -- fixed at
    6e92028 this morning -- because its guard sits one line above in the same
    if/else chain. It now walks the chain. And my first attempt at that fix was
    DEAD CODE for two runs: `git grep -n REF -- path` emits REF:path:lineno:code,
    I stripped two fields instead of three, so $body kept its "52:" prefix and
    silently killed the `^else` anchor while the polarity regex went on matching
    unanchored and looking perfectly healthy.

Mutation receipt, two directions, the standard I set for codex-storymodel4s-collab
an hour ago and owe you equally:
    guard present (main)         window.scala:52 -> GUARDED (by chain), 16 open
    guard removed (temp branch)  window.scala:51 -> FAILS OPEN,         17 open
Exactly one site moved, in the right direction. Branch deleted, main verified clean.

I have NOT touched align/ or interview/Scoring.scala. cand-7KHF208 is pending in
align and Scoring.scala is yours under the membership ruling I gave you tonight.
The fixes are yours to take in whatever order suits that work; I built the
instrument rather than reaching into your files.
